english: And accordingly we should expound the Adhikaraṇa in the following manner Question to be dealt with In a case where a thing, having its origin that thing be equipped with the properties peculiar to the former Veda, or with those of the latter? Pūrvapaksha Inasmuch as the origination of a thing always precedes its application, the properties employed should be those of the Veda in which it has its origin. Siddhanta The properties should be those of that Veda which lays down its application because the origination of a thing is only for the sake of the uses to which it may be applied because it is only when the thing in questionthe Sāmasingingis applied to use that it stands in need of some tone to be applied to it and hence the tones enjoined in the Injunction Uccuiḥ rca,etc. are those that are perceived at the time of usage, and not at the time of the origination as there is no injunction of its being brought into action at that time.
